title: Fourth moment bound for degree-one polynomials
statement: Let $\Omega_i$ be a finite probability space for each coordinate $i$ of an $n$-coordinate product, and let $X_i$ be a real-valued random variable on $\Omega_i$. Suppose each $X_i$ has mean zero and third moment zero, and its fourth moment is at most three times the square of its second moment. For any multilinear polynomial in these variables of degree at most one, under the independent product distribution its fourth moment is at most three times the square of its second moment.
